governed_construct: A function definition whose name marks it as an initialization function, i.e. whose name begins with 'init' (case-insensitive): function declarations, named function expressions or arrow functions bound to a variable, class methods, object-literal methods/properties whose value is a function, and functions assigned to a member (e.g. module.exports.X = function...). Calls, imports, and non-function bindings (e.g. an 'initialized' boolean field, an 'initialState' object) are not instances.
interpretation: An initialization function is identified by its name starting with 'init' in any case (init, initX, InitX, initializeX, InitializeX, Initializer...). It conforms only if its name is exactly 'Initialize' followed by a non-empty PascalCase category, i.e. matches ^Initialize[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ (e.g. InitializeHandlers). Abbreviated forms (initHandlers, InitDatabase), camelCase (initializeQueue), and bare 'Initialize'/'init' with no category violate. Only definitions count; calls to or imports of init-prefixed functions defined elsewhere are not instances, and identifiers that merely start with 'init' but are not bound to a function (initialized, initialState) are not instances. Mentions in comments or strings are ignored. Functions with other setup-like names (setup, bootstrap, configure) are not treated as initialization functions, since the rule is a naming rule and only the init-prefix gives a deterministic reading.
